name: UK Biobank Eye and Vision / UK Biobank Repeat Imaging
institution: UK Biobank; UK Biobank Eye and Vision Consortium
year: 2022 (online publication of retinal grading report; print 2023)
citation: Warwick AN et al. UK Biobank retinal imaging grading: methodology, baseline characteristics and findings for common ocular diseases. Eye. Online 2022; print 2023 (PubMed 36329166; correction 36604558).
modalities: Fundus; OCT; brain MRI in a subset
images: Aug 2025 Showcase, 102,971 left-eye field items and 104,504 right-eye field items across instances; counts include repeats. Historical 2009–2010 grading paper reports 121,260 gradable eyes.
participants: 2009–2010: 68,514 attended, 68,504 had ≥1 CFP; 64,367 had ≥1 gradable CFP. Not the all-instances union.
eyes: Left/right coded separately; unilateral missingness possible.
device: Topcon 3D OCT-1000 Mark II; single-field 45° CFP (baseline reported protocol).
quality: Separate grades; gradeable denominators differ by eye and endpoint.
multivisit: Yes; Showcase instances per eye. Repeated observations apply only to a subset.
multimodal: Yes; OCT + CFP, brain MRI in an overlapping subset.
multicenter: Yes; recruitment/assessment centres, imaging availability varies by centre and instance.
relation: Cohort family; eye, brain, repeat assessment, outcome subsets and secondary papers are overlapping facets.
image_access: Confirmed bulk CFP/OCT data fields under approved UKB-RAP project; new applications paused on cited page.
label_access: Confirmed controlled participant-level linkage, depending on approved tier/fields and consent.
license: UK Biobank project agreement; not an open image licence.
research_terms: Eligible researchers, public-interest health research, approved project, institutional agreement and fees; RAP compute/storage costs additional.
commercial_terms: Eligible scientific researchers in commercial organisations can apply on the public-interest health-research terms; no general commercial reuse right.
pairing: Approved project participant ID + assessment instance + laterality for retinal bulk fields. Define imaging index date and match hospital/death follow-up or MRI instance explicitly. 46,969 people passed QC in a historical age/stroke study (35,917 held out after healthy age-training group); not the whole UKB or the eye–MRI intersection.
strengths: Published same-participant outcomes across age, stroke, OCT–MRI, dementia and PD; separated eye fields and repeat instances.
limitations: New application intake shown as paused at 2026-11-03 (planned late-2026 opening is not confirmation); selection by imaging/QC/healthy volunteer and different exam dates. Age gap is a prediction residual; individual biological age is not ground truth.
experiment: Train a patient-split chronological-age model in the disease-free baseline subset. Estimate independent age-bias correction; compare a clinical stroke-risk baseline against baseline+age gap under time-to-event analysis with an external cohort. Audit MRI temporal offsets, withdrawals and follow-up.

name: NHANES 2005–2008 Ophthalmology – Retinal Imaging (OPXRET_D / OPXRET_E)
institution: CDC, NCHS; University of Wisconsin reading centre
year: 2008 (first release of 2005–2006 codebook); next independent 2007–2008 cycle also included.
citation: CDC/NCHS. NHANES 2005–2006 and 2007–2008, Ophthalmology – Retinal Imaging, OPXRET_D/E codebooks.
participants: 5,371 had gradable retinal photographs across the two cycles in a published stroke analysis; 4,570 had its required stroke and eye variables. Not total recruited.
eyes: Protocol two 45° fields per eye, both eyes.
resolution: 6.3 MP image capture (not necessarily released pixel dimensions).
quality: Reading-centre graders; per-eye gradability fields; analytic sample excludes ungradable cases.
multivisit: Two independent survey cross-sections; mortality linkage extends follow-up. No repeated retinal imaging documented for the same respondents.
multicenter: National clustered multistage sampling; mobile exam locations do not imply released centre IDs.
relation: Two independent continuous-NHANES cycles grouped as one resource; not NHANES III or the derived myopia/metal exposure entry.
image_access: Unknown for raw TIFFs; official open OPXRET files are derived XPT tables, not images. Acquisition manual describes historical TIFF creation only.
label_access: Confirmed open respondent-level grading, demographic and questionnaire variables; public-use NDI-linked mortality restricted in detail.
research_terms: Use public-use documentation, design/weights, codebooks and cycle-specific rules; raw pixel access separately unverified.
pairing: SEQN keys within corresponding OPXRET_D/E, DEMO_D/E, MCQ_D/E and public LMF files. Sampling weights and design variables mandatory. MCQ160F is self-reported stroke history, MCQ180F age first told. Public mortality includes limited fields and disclosure protection; no incident non-fatal stroke demonstrated.
strengths: Independently reproducible participant-level analysis using open retinal grades and mortality/medical questionnaires; probability sampling.
limitations: No confirmed public raw image route. No verified brain MRI or contemporaneous standard dementia battery in the retinal cycles. Cross-cycle cognition data cannot be joined by respondent.
experiment: Use public OPXRET grades as exposures for survey-weighted prevalent self-reported stroke and time-to-death. Restrict to eligible adults, combine cycles correctly, estimate total eligible-to-complete attrition; pixel-level age model requires separately verified images.

name: NHANES III (1988–1994) fundus grading and NDI linkage
citation: CDC/NCHS. Third National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey, Examination Data File documentation; NHANES III Fundus Photography Manual.
eyes: One randomly selected eye, one nonstereoscopic colour photograph.
participants: 7,640 adults in one eye–mortality study; not a count of all retinal photographs.
quality: Reading-centre grades; images may be ungradable.
multivisit: Cross-sectional photography; death follow-up by NDI.
multimodal: Fundus + health exam and mortality records
multicenter: US probability sample; site availability for modelling unknown.
relation: Separate survey era from 2005–2008; different participants and single-eye acquisition protocol.
image_access: Unknown for raw photographs. Exam public file contains coded retinal readings.
label_access: Confirmed public exam and NDI files for linked respondent-level analysis.
research_terms: Apply survey sampling rules and use matching release documentation.
pairing: NHANES III public exam participant ID links within NHANES III and NDI mortality, not to a different continuous cycle. Directly demonstrated in 7,640 adults.
strengths: National probability survey and prospective linked mortality, independent of later NHANES.
limitations: Single historical film eye, nonrepresentative of pediatric or younger ages, raw image transfer not established.
experiment: Independently replicate grade–mortality associations across NHANES eras after harmonizing grading, monocular vs binocular ascertainment, case mix, follow-up and survey weights.

name: Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) retinal ancillary studies
institution: NHLBI; ARIC Coordinating Center, University of North Carolina and four field communities
citation: Wong TY et al. Cerebral white matter lesions, retinopathy, and incident clinical stroke. JAMA. 2002;288:67–74. See also retinal-stroke analysis, PMID 11597667 (2001).
modalities: Fundus; later OCT/OCTA-related ancillary eye variables; brain MRI in a subset
participants: 10,358 retinal photography participants in early stroke study; 1,684 with MRI+retina in 1993–1995 study. These are distinct analytic denominators.
eyes: Visit 3 single-eye protocol, later visits/ancillary forms distinguish eyes.
quality: Grading and ungradable/exclusion fields; later ancillary dictionary also distinguishes retina, GCC, ONH and macular/disc angio scans by eye.
multivisit: Yes; visit 3 and visit 5 CFP; MRI repeat subset and follow-up. Do not assume each participant has serial imaging.
multimodal: Yes; CFP + brain MRI in overlapping participants.
relation: V3, V5 neurocognitive, V7 ancillary and later endpoints belong to overlapping ARIC family.
image_access: Uncertain for raw retinal/brain images via standard BioLINCC release. Public data dictionary documents study IDs, derived measures and flags, not distribution of image files.
label_access: Confirmed application route for exam, annual follow-up, adjudicated event and ancillary variables; verify selected release/fields.
license: BioLINCC Research Materials Distribution Agreement (RMDA); no open pixel licence verified.
research_terms: Register PI/submit study request and institution/ethics requirements per BioLINCC. BioLINCC/NIH controlled-access route prohibits covered access from institutions located in China (including Hong Kong/Macau) and the other listed countries under NOT-OD-25-083. A separate study collaboration is not a verified alternative route for covered data.
pairing: Use cohort ID / visit-mapped scrambled ID supplied in approved release (visit-specific ID in ancillary dictionary); ascertain phenotype availability by visit. 1,684 actually had both retinal exam and brain MRI, not all 15,792 parent participants.
strengths: Direct correspondence among retinal signs, WML/infarcts, later clinical stroke, cognitive test trajectories and study-defined dementia.
limitations: Eye photos vs already derived grades, visit-specific laterality, censoring and late-visit survivor selection. Raw image package unconfirmed; check ancillary PI and linkage/consent.
experiment: Compare baseline clinical model vs model adding retinal signs to predict first clinical stroke, quantify added calibration/discrimination at a fixed horizon and separately model MRI lesions; repeat cognition analyses accounting for attrition.

name: Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA Eye / cognitive–MRI ancillaries)
institution: NHLBI; MESA Coordinating Center and six US field communities
citation: Kawasaki R et al. Retinal microvascular signs and risk of stroke: the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis. Stroke. 2012. Compare Ong SS et al., Alzheimers Dement. DOI 10.1002/alz.13498.
participants: 4,849 underwent retinal photography in 2002–04 stroke study (62 incident strokes over 6 years). North Carolina MRI/cognition subset: 313 with gradable exam-2 images; 306 with gradable exam-5 images (overlapping groups).
eyes: Both eyes photographed under protocol; a usable fellow eye may replace ungradable measurement.
device: Canon CR6-45NM with digital Canon D-60 camera back for early retinal photography.
quality: Reading-centre grading, QC and gradable subsets; laterality fallback must be reported.
multivisit: Yes; fundus at exams 2 and 5; cognitive/MRI assessments later.
multimodal: Yes; same-participant CFP and brain MRI in NC subset.
multicenter: Yes; six communities for parent; specific paired MRI results derive from one NC field centre.
relation: Retinal, cognitive and MRI ancillaries overlap parent. Do not sum exam-specific denominators.
image_access: Uncertain for archived retinal pixel files; BioLINCC route is for datasets; MESA ancillary project required for new analyses using stored source images when beyond released data.
label_access: Confirmed mechanism for deidentified data through BioLINCC/DMDA and direct MESA proposals; exact data source selection subject to review.
license: MESA DMDA / BioLINCC agreement depending on route.
research_terms: BioLINCC application or MESA manuscript proposal/committee approval; extra Coordinating Center services or reanalysis of existing images may require ancillary proposal. BioLINCC/NIH controlled-access route prohibits covered access from institutions located in China (including Hong Kong/Macau) and the other listed countries under NOT-OD-25-083. A separate study collaboration is not a verified alternative route for covered data.
pairing: Same participants with eye images at exams 2/5 and cognition at exam 5 or MRI/cognition at exam 6. Use MESA participant and exam linkage after approval; not all six centres contributed the directly documented MRI subset.
strengths: Multiethnic prospective cohort with proven retina–event and retina–brain pairings, repeated CFP in a subset.
limitations: 62 early clinical strokes despite 4,849 people; MRI ancillary subset and parent centre distribution differ. Raw pixel transfer unverified.
experiment: Externally validate a frozen retinal vascular/age score on subsequent stroke, compare calibration by population group. Analyze NC baseline fundus vs later MRI/cognition separately, with lag and attrition reported.

name: Cardiovascular Health Study (CHS) retinal examination
citation: Associations between findings on cranial magnetic resonance imaging and retinal photography in the elderly: the Cardiovascular Health Study. Am J Epidemiol. 2007;165:78–84. PMID 17041135.
participants: 1,717 with retinal examination plus brain MRI. 2,211 with retinal photography in cognition/dementia analysis; denominators overlap. CHD/stroke caliber study had 1,992 gradable.
eyes: One randomly selected eye at 1997–98 visit; 45° disc–macula field.
quality: 832/2,824 had ungradable photos for caliber in a published analysis; selected sample of older survivors.
multivisit: Longitudinal clinical events; MRI progression assessed. Repeated fundus photos not verified.
multicenter: Yes; US field sites; see BioLINCC and published field-centre covariate.
relation: One cohort; MRI, cognitive and event analyses partially overlap.
image_access: Uncertain for raw retinal or brain pixels; NIH describes their acquisition and provides data/ancillaries, not a retinal-image manifest.
label_access: Confirmed BioLINCC study request; grades and follow-up documented; exact approved outcome dictionary and visit match should be checked.
license: BioLINCC RMDA, not a verified image redistribution licence.
research_terms: PI registration, application, institutional agreement/ethics requirements. BioLINCC/NIH controlled-access route prohibits covered access from institutions located in China (including Hong Kong/Macau) and the other listed countries under NOT-OD-25-083. A separate study collaboration is not a verified alternative route for covered data. Data/biospecimen use is consent-tiered to CVD-related research only or unrestricted research area; a non-CVD neurodegeneration or aging project must confirm its permitted subset.
pairing: 1,717 participants underwent MRI and retinal photography in 1991–99; eye date was not necessarily MRI date. Separate patient subset had cognition/dementia adjudication. Use study ID + visit, document baseline and follow-up.
strengths: Older population; multiple verified endpoints including subsequent CHD/stroke, MRI infarcts and white matter grade, cognitive tests and dementia.
limitations: One randomly chosen eye; substantial missing/poor-quality photos; selected older population and uncertain pixel release.
experiment: Externally validate published retinal/clinical risk scores in older adults using subsequent adjudicated stroke and MRI white-matter grade as separate outcomes. Report missingness and age-distribution shift.

name: Framingham Eye Study (FES I/II), Original Framingham Heart Study cohort
institution: Framingham Heart Study, Boston University/NHLBI; University of Wisconsin photograph reading centre
citation: The Framingham Eye Study monograph. Surv Ophthalmol. 1980. PMID 7444756; NIH dbGaP FES II original-cohort eye exam protocol.
participants: 2,631 aged 52–85 in the 1973–75 clinical eye monograph. Approximately 1,500 surviving participants were targeted by FES II protocol; not a verified complete paired/gradable photo count.
eyes: FES II protocol grades right and left eye photographs; disc and macula; visit-level image quality.
quality: Reading centre forms and slide-set quality control. Historical analogue slides.
multivisit: FES I/II photographed survivors: 1973–75 and 1986–89 exam protocol. Individual paired usable count unknown.
multimodal: Fundus + eye/clinical examination. No demonstrated paired brain MRI here.
multicenter: Single community (Framingham, MA); multiple reading/processing institutes do not imply multisite population recruitment.
relation: Original cohort only. Do not transfer Offspring MRI/AD sample names or counts without validating the same individuals.
image_access: Uncertain for digitised source photographs. Protocol specifies archived slides; data package is clinical/ancillary data, no confirmed photo inventory.
label_access: Confirmed original-cohort selected eye data through study application; candidate event/MRI cross-joins require approved file inventory.
license: Institutional BioLINCC/Framingham study agreements; no open image licence verified.
research_terms: Full or expedited IRB/ethics approval required. Exemption/waiver does not suffice according to BioLINCC. BioLINCC/NIH controlled-access route prohibits covered access from institutions located in China (including Hong Kong/Macau) and the other listed countries under NOT-OD-25-083. A separate study collaboration is not a verified alternative route for covered data.
pairing: FES II original-cohort photo grading forms and visit/person records; verify digital scan inventory and subject crosswalk before requesting image–endpoint set. Distinct from offspring/OMNI.
strengths: Repeated macular assessment across decades and an original longitudinal cardiovascular cohort.
limitations: Survivor/age selection, analogue films; diagnostic/findings tables publicly documented but raw image retrieval, paired MRI/clinical stroke intersections unresolved.
experiment: Seek a feasibility count for original-cohort photographs that can be digitised and matched across FES visits to age and clinical event records before attempting image-based modeling.

hypertension: BP measurements documented; clinical hypertension label not verified.

name: Age, Gene/Environment Susceptibility–Reykjavik Study (AGES-RS)
institution: Icelandic Heart Association and US National Institute on Aging
citation: Qiu C et al. Cerebral microbleeds, retinopathy, and dementia: the AGES-Reykjavik Study. Neurology. 2010;75:2221–2228.
participants: 5,764 AGES-I parent; 3,906 in joint retina/cognition/MRI cross-section; 2,502 in baseline retina with serial MRI microbleed study. 4,966 in separate retina–mortality analysis; samples overlap.
eyes: Both eyes; two 45° fields/eye centred on disc and fovea after pharmacologic dilation.
quality: Standardised image grading; require gradable image/assessment for specific analytic cohorts.
multivisit: Yes for brain MRI; baseline CFP and 2007–11 MRI follow-up documented. Repeat retinal images in that paired analysis not established.
relation: AGES I/II are successive phases in surviving Reykjavik participants; analysis Ns overlap.
image_access: Uncertain for original retinal/MRI pixel transfer. DUA collaboration is documented for individual-level AGES data; file-specific availability/onsite calculation must be confirmed.
label_access: Research collaboration and approval through Icelandic Heart Association/AGES Executive Committee; raw image list and crosswalk not public.
license: Negotiated collaboration/DUA; no public individual-level licence identified.
research_terms: Submit project to Icelandic Heart Association (AGES_data_request@hjarta.is; recent study data-availability statement), consent and institutional requirements apply.
pairing: Exams from same elderly participants at AGES-I; separate study identifies 2,502 who also had repeat MRI at AGES-II. Outcomes and dates are cohort managed, so confirm ID mapping and maximum allowed visit lag.
strengths: Direct fundus–MRI microbleed, clinical AD/vascular dementia adjudication, cognition and death ascertainment with population controls.
limitations: Elderly survivors from a geographically concentrated population; most dementia evidence cited is cross-sectional. Eligibility for a data collaboration is not proof that image files can be transferred.
experiment: Study whether baseline retinal microvascular signs improve prediction of new MRI-defined microbleeds by location. Separate cross-sectional AD/vascular dementia analyses; use Icelandic cohort as external test only if data agreement permits.

A: Chronological age and photos in older persons, limited age span.
B: Prior stroke history paired with retinal status in mortality analysis; not evidence for incident clinical stroke subtype prediction.
C: Bilateral fundus at baseline with two brain MRI waves on same people.
D: Cognition and clinical dementia subtypes assessed in same people.
G: Multimodal older-adult external cohort; single centre, pixels unverified.

stroke_type: Prior stroke considered; subtype classification not established.
stroke_time: Prior stroke, not verified onset date.
brain_mri: MRI in retina-imaged participants at two waves.
ad: Clinical AD criteria, not biomarker-positive AD.
cognition: Processing speed, memory and executive performance.
followup: Serial MRI, separate from death follow-up.

name: Scottish Collaborative Optometry-Ophthalmology Network e-research (SCONe)
institution: University of Edinburgh, Scottish community optometry practices, Public Health Scotland/eDRIS National Safe Haven
citation: Tochel C et al. SCONe: a community-acquired retinal image repository enabling ocular, cardiovascular and neurodegenerative disease prediction. BMJ Health Care Inform. 2025;32:e101236.
images: Phase-2 report: 1,499,677 images delivered; nearly 800,000 linked to NHS records at that report. Earlier published cohort: >367,000 matched images. Distinct snapshots, not additive.
participants: 131,678 people in phase-2 delivery; linked person count not given for the ~800,000 image update. 2025 descriptor reports >36,000 matched patients.
eyes: Usually left + right per date; coded outcomes assigned to the person, not eye-specific.
device: 2025 subset: typically 45° CFP; Topcon (~90%), Canon (~5%), Nikon (~4%). Device shares should not be generalized to all future submissions.
quality: Approximately 9,500 images read for AMD, quality and pathology in phase-2 report; not all images clinically graded.
multivisit: Yes, repeated community optometry dates for some individuals; date/follow-up heterogeneity.
multimodal: Fundus + healthcare records. Neither routine brain MRI nor OCT pixels established by cohort descriptor.
multicenter: Yes; multiple community optometry practices and camera systems across Scotland.
relation: Phase 1/2 and 2025 published linked subset overlap. No additional cohort for each practice or outcome.
image_access: Confirmed within Scottish National Safe Haven for approved SCONe researchers/projects only. External researchers need a project-specific partnership; raw export not offered.
label_access: Confirmed linked coded hospital/general ophthalmic/death records for approved Safe Haven work; not an open individual-level table.
license: Public Health Scotland governance; no publicly redistributable patient/image licence.
research_terms: Collaborative inquiry with SCONe, approved institution/research project, governance training and Safe Haven-controlled analysis; only checked non-disclosive outputs can leave.
pairing: PHS/eDRIS links images via approved patient identity matching to routine health records. Research uses deidentified person, image date and earliest disease-code date (clinical onset unknown). More than one image/eye/date possible. Linked subset is smaller than phase-2 delivered inventory.
strengths: Direct clinical-code linkage for stroke, clinical AD/dementia and PD; repeated fundus, multiple devices and spatially distributed community sites.
limitations: Optometry attenders, older population and incomplete medical history. First code is a dated proxy; do not assume it is incident onset or model same-day dual-eye images as independent people. Safe Haven access is project specific.
experiment: On an approved Safe Haven project, train a patient-split age model and evaluate whether a frozen age gap improves prediction of first recorded stroke/dementia beyond clinical covariates. Require adequate pre-index observation, treat death as competing risk, reserve a practice/device and monitor coding completeness.

B: Table 2 verifies same patients with coded stroke and retina, relative first-code dates.

age: Individual ages linked to capture dates; cohort access is controlled.
sex: Patient demographics in linked health records.
cardiovascular: Ischaemic heart disease, hypertension/heart disease and pulmonary heart disease codes.

ad: Clinical AD code, not gold-standard pathology.

name: Lothian Birth Cohort 1936 (LBC1936) retinal and brain imaging
institution: University of Edinburgh, Lothian Birth Cohorts
citation: Retinal microvasculature and cerebral small vessel disease in the Lothian Birth Cohort 1936 and Mild Stroke Study. Sci Rep. 2019. PMID 31004095.
participants: Wave 2: 866 attended clinical assessment, 681 completed brain imaging and provided WMH/SVD data; analytic n=603 with retinal measurements in both eyes. Separate retina–cognition study n=683. Do not add Mild Stroke Study n=155.
device: Non-mydriatic 45° Canon CR-DGi CFP in Wave 2.
quality: Use bilateral gradeable vessel metrics for the 603-person MRI analysis; exclusions can bias complete-case subset.
multivisit: Yes for longitudinal cognitive testing, from childhood IQ through late-life waves; retinal vascular measures in cited studies were acquired at wave 2, repeated retinal pixels not demonstrated.
multimodal: Yes; bilateral CFP + structural brain MRI.
multicenter: One regional community cohort (Lothian, Scotland); not multicenter retinal acquisition evidence.
relation: Not LBC1921. Mild Stroke Study is a distinct cohort sharing a paper/imaging protocol; n=155 must not be attributed to LBC1936.
image_access: Uncertain for raw retinal pixels under standard request. Official study publishes dictionaries and a study-specific data request form; source pixel access and redistribution require explicit confirmation.
label_access: Confirmed proposal-based route for cohort/imaging variables, pending approval and approved release field inventory.
license: Cohort-specific agreement, no open raw-image licence identified.
research_terms: List proposed variables and methods, submit LBC data request form to cohort director; verify retinal pixel coverage and which sites are eligible.
pairing: 1936-born cohort wave 2 (~age 73), bilateral fundus vascular measures and structural MRI. Subsequent cognitive scores link to the same people. Do not transfer stroke patients or counts from companion Mild Stroke Study.
strengths: Narrow age range controls age confounding; measured childhood cognitive ability and later-life repeated tests, MRI small-vessel phenotypes.
limitations: Birth-year restriction precludes learning a widely generalizable age clock within this sample. Image transfer not established. Secondary prevention/mild-stroke patients from another study must be kept separate.
experiment: Use as an external test of retinal vessel features for WMH burden and late-life cognitive change at nearly fixed age. Compare against baseline IQ and vascular risk, model mortality/attrition, and avoid misclassifying longitudinal cognitive tests as dementia diagnoses.
